plaintiff.occupation_before: Self-employed man collecting rubbish from a number of multi-storey buildings
plaintiff.occupation_after: Has not worked since the date of the accident

injuries.description: compound fracture of the right tibia and fibula
source: he had suffered a compound fracture of the right tibia and fibula.

injuries.description: ½ inch shortening of the leg
source: there is a ½ inch shortening of the leg with a restriction of ankle joint movement.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injuries to the ankle or foot

source: The plaintiff is left with extensive scarring

manifestations.description: The wound continued to discharge until March 1982
underwent considerable pain and discomfort in hospital
has not worked since the date of the accident

The resulting impairment of the right leg is assessed by Dr Wedderburn as 7% from shortening and 9% from loss of ankle joint movement. That is a 16% impairment of the leg and a 6% impairment of the whole man. In view of the plaintiff's occupation at the time of the accident Dr Wedderburn would classify the impairment as a 15% disability.

treatments_received: operation on 19th September securing the tibia with a bone plate and screws
cross flap procedure (flap of skin raised on the opposite leg and placed to cover the open wound, legs bandaged together and held by a plaster cast for about three weeks)
division and suturing of the flap; suturing of donor site
split skin graft with skin taken from the front of his right thigh
attended at intervals at the South Kwai Chung Clinic
hospital treatment at Princess Margaret Hospital

losses.description: Pain, Suffering and Loss of Amenities; the plaintiff's wound continued to discharge for some three years, he underwent considerable pain and discomfort in hospital and is unable to squat. Award under this head assessed at $60,000.
Unable ever to resume former occupation as collector of rubbish because of his disability and age; future earnings under this head assessed at $108,000.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wan Shui Yee v along Ying Tak and Hwang Jing Miu Jimmy
comparable_cases.injury_description: Agreed figure of $35,000 under this head in a somewhat similar case
